action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The long-run uptrend is intact, so the model keeps the posture at scale up, but apply it carefully: Bitcoin is about 8% under its 50-day average and only about 3% above its 200-day average, and no rally or drop window is open. Keep growth in small steps that are easy to pause, lead with trust and explainer messages, and only speed up acquisition if price closes back above $81,417 (the 50-day average). A close below $73,149 is the point to review the posture and shift weight toward keeping existing users.

analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds, but the coming week looks soft to neutral and price is sitting just above the line that matters most. At about $75,038, Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 20 days, sits about 8% below it and about 11% below its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 32 (fear), even though many people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money. A normal week swings about $2,926, so a close above $76,500 (top of a typical week's swing) would turn it clearly up, a close below $73,149 (the 200-day average) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy. US inflation data due today (PANews) is the near-term event to watch; a close under $73,149 is the cue for safety-first messaging.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 18% higher and about 93% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 10%, and news is taking a little off, with a crypto-skeptical senator, Elizabeth Warren, set to chair the Senate Banking Committee (PANews). Price must win back $81,417 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there room to climb further; while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading. The next Fed meeting is on 8 December, so keep bigger campaign pushes for a reclaim of the 50-day average.

The 3-6 month picture leans up at a moderate strength. Price is about 3% above its 200-day average, which is still rising about 5% over 90 days, and news is adding a little: UK banks can now apply to run crypto businesses and Coinbase received a US national trust charter (PANews). The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,149 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,601 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. A close below the 200-day average is what would weaken this picture and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.

items.theme: Wall Street moves stocks onto blockchains
items.why: The New York Stock Exchange says it will use the Avalanche blockchain to settle tokenized stocks, Formation plans a tokenized securities venue on Solana, and Charles Schwab's crypto arm added SOL, AVAX and LINK trading.
